Uninsured Motorist Coverage in Florida: Why It's More Important Than Ever

May 7, 2026 · FloridAuto.com

Florida consistently ranks among the top states in the country for uninsured drivers. Estimates suggest that between 20–26% of Florida drivers are on the road without liability insurance at any given time. That's roughly 1 in 4 cars you pass on I-4 or the Turnpike.

What Happens If an Uninsured Driver Hits You?

If an uninsured driver causes an accident and injures you, your PIP coverage kicks in first — but PIP only covers 80% of medical bills up to $10,000. For serious injuries, that's a drop in the bucket. Without Uninsured Motorist (UM) coverage, you'd have to sue the at-fault driver personally — and most people driving without insurance don't have assets worth pursuing.

What UM Coverage Does

Uninsured Motorist coverage steps into the shoes of the at-fault driver's missing liability insurance. It pays for:

  • Medical bills above and beyond your PIP limit
  • Pain and suffering (UM can pay this; PIP cannot)
  • Lost wages beyond the PIP 60% threshold
  • Long-term rehabilitation costs

UM coverage also protects you against underinsured drivers — those who have some insurance, but not enough to cover the full cost of your injuries.

Stacked vs. Unstacked UM Coverage

In Florida, you can choose between stacked and unstacked UM coverage. Stacked UM means your coverage limits multiply across the number of vehicles on your policy — so two cars with $100,000 UM each gives you $200,000 in protection. Unstacked keeps each vehicle's limit separate. Stacked costs more but offers significantly stronger protection.

How Much UM Should You Carry?

At a minimum, match your UM limits to your liability limits. Many insurance professionals recommend carrying at least $100,000/$300,000 in UM coverage, especially if you drive frequently or have a long commute in high-traffic areas.
